title: Pick's Theorem OQ-01-OQ-01: Primitive Lattice Triangle Decomposition
description: Proves every non-degenerate lattice triangle can be decomposed into exactly |det| primitive lattice triangles (each with |det|=1, area=1/2). Key missing ingredient for the constructive proof of Pick's theorem via triangulation. 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Pick's theorem (1899): for a lattice polygon, Area = I + B/2 − 1. The constructive proof decomposes into triangles, requiring that each lattice triangle subdivides into |det| primitive triangles. This file formalizes that key lemma.
overview.problemStatement: Prove: every non-degenerate lattice triangle with determinant d decomposes into exactly |d| primitive lattice triangles (those with |det|=1).
overview.proofStrategy: Strong induction on |det(T)|. Base case: |det|=1 means T is already primitive. Inductive step: exists_reduction (lattice basis reduction) gives a smaller triangle. Edge-splitting det additivity: det(T) = det(T₁) + det(T₂) for edge split. Decompose by induction on each piece.
keyInsights: **Primitive triangle characterization**: |det|=1 ↔ area=1/2 ↔ no interior or boundary points (besides vertices).
**Det additivity**: splitting a triangle T along an interior lattice edge gives det(T) = det(T₁) + det(T₂). Induction proceeds on the sum.
**Reduction**: any non-primitive triangle has an interior lattice point on an edge, giving a smaller sub-triangle with smaller |det|.

sections.title: Primitive Triangulation via Strong Induction
sections.summary: LatticeTriangle structure. LatticeTriangle.det, IsPrimitive. exists_primitive_triangulation by strong induction on |det|. Concrete verification examples.
sections.mathContext: Every lattice triangle $T$ with $|\det T| = d$ decomposes into $d$ primitive lattice triangles.

conclusion.summary: 17 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Primitive lattice triangulation proved by strong induction on determinant.
conclusion.implications: This lemma is the key ingredient for the constructive proof of Pick's theorem. It shows that the area of a lattice polygon is completely determined by its lattice point counts.
openQuestions: Can the full Pick's theorem be derived from this decomposition?
Can the primitive triangulation be generalized to higher-dimensional lattice simplices?
Can the lattice basis reduction used in exists_reduction be formalized from scratch?
